title: Hierarchical Clustering
interviewAnswer: Hierarchical clustering repeatedly merges or splits clusters and produces a dendrogram. Linkage choice defines how inter-cluster distance is measured and can strongly change results.
why: Hierarchical Clustering appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Hierarchical clustering repeatedly merges or splits clusters and produces a dendrogram. Linkage choice defines how inter-cluster distance is measured and can strongly change results. Single/complete/average/Ward linkage behave differently. Scaling features matters. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Cluster products by standardized usage profiles and inspect multiple cut levels in the dendrogram.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Hierarchical Clustering make?
How would you validate or debug Hierarchical Clustering in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
